marco-support: FYI customer reported sudden mTLS handshake failures to Private control plane after they rolled a new egress ACL this morning. They see ~30% of connections fail, others succeed.

jenna-sre: Can you paste the s_client output and a pcap? Also which control plane endpoint/IP?

marco-support: Endpoint: cp-01.private.redwood.example.com (34.198.12.45). Customer ran:

```
openssl s_client -connect 34.198.12.45:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -tls1_3 -msg -debug
```

Output snippet when it fails: 

```
>>> TLS 1.3, Handshake [length 0148]
<<< TLS 1.3, Handshake [length 0001]
*** SSL handshake has read 65 bytes and written 389 bytes
*** error:1425F102:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:wrong version number
```

and sometimes: `ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher`

They attached tcpdump from their egress NAT showing client_hello split across two packets (frag at 1460):

```
12:34:56.789 IP a.b.c.d.52345 > 34.198.12.45.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, len 1460
12:34:56.790 IP a.b.c.d. > 34.198.12.45.443: Flags [P.], seq 1461:1540, len 79
```

They said their new firewall adjusts MSS and also does TLS inspection for some hosts.

alex-eng: Hmm looks like the client_hello gets fragmented and the upstream (control plane) sees only first fragment missing extensions (signature_algorithms, key_share) which matter for TLS1.3. If TLS inspection or a proxy drops the second fragment, server can't negotiate.

luis-netops: Customer confirms traffic passes through a PaloAlto cluster that does SSL forward proxy. After the ACL change the proxy started applying inspection to that CIDR.

jenna-sre: Ok. Repro steps we want them to run: 1) capture tshark on their egress before the proxy (raw client) and after the proxy (to see rewrite). 2) run openssl s_client with -tlsextdebug -msg to show which extensions arrive. 3) try connecting to control plane IP directly from a host bypassing proxy/NAT if possible.

marco-support: I asked them to run:

```
# from a host behind proxy
openssl s_client -connect 34.198.12.45:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -tlsextdebug -msg -debug > sclient.log 2>&1
# on egress gateway
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/egress.pcap host 34.198.12.45 and port 443
```

They uploaded sclient.log and a small pcap. Analysis notes: first ClientHello present on wire only contains legacy_version and no extensions in the first fragment, second fragment has extensions. Proxy seems to drop/strip second fragment occasionally.

alex-eng: If the proxy reassembles TLS but has a bug for large ClientHello (e.g., many SANs or long cert chain), it might mishandle fragments. Could also be MTU/MSS mismatch causing middlebox to drop non-initial fragments.

luis-netops: Workarounds to propose to customer: 1) add control plane IPs to egress allowlist/inspection bypass so the proxy won't touch TLS for those flows. 2) If bypass not possible, have proxy vendor check SSL-forward-proxy patch for ClientHello fragmentation or increase TCP reassembly buffers. 3) Temporarily reduce TLS client_hello size (remove unnecessary SANs) — not ideal for them.

jenna-sre: Also request they try forcing TLS1.2 as a short repro to see if handshake succeeds consistently (older TLS sometimes has smaller CH). Command: `-tls1_2` in openssl. If TLS1.2 succeeds consistently, that supports missing TLS1.3 ext issue.

marco-support: Customer tried TLS1.2 and it mostly worked. They also did a direct curl from a host with policy bypass and it worked.

alex-eng: Good data point. Engineering note: control plane currently requires TLS1.3 client key_share ext for performance; we can accept TLS1.2 fallback but that increases CPU and maybe not acceptable as a long-term fix. Recommend bypass/whitelist.

jenna-sre: I filed a request to engage security/netops at the customer's side and suggested a temporary bypass. Also pinged the proxy vendor with their pcap.

luis-netops: I'll add a suggested diagnostic packet to give vendor: run tcpdump with `-s 0 -w` and include the first 3 packets of a failed handshake, plus `openssl s_client -connect ... -tlsextdebug -msg`. Vendors usually ask for that.

marco-support: Customer accepted bypass for control plane IPs and reports errors dropped to ~0. Recommending we keep monitoring for 24h and then close.

jenna-sre: Thanks. Action items: - support to confirm bypass applied and monitor (marco-support) - eng to consider adding better TLS1.2 fallback metrics/logs on control plane (alex-eng) - file internal KB about client_hello fragmentation and SSL-FW proxies (jenna-sre).

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.17/patch-ctrlplane-tls-fallback queued by alex-eng :white_check_mark:

marco-support: Will close thread after 24h clean. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
